note: [L] carries the cited triangularity as the field Push.Local.Leading.triangular (bundled into the MergeProof.Triangle hypothesis with the marked error), and uses it in Columns.triangular_high, inv_triangular_high and low_le. Difference: it is a structure field in contrapositive form (nonzero entry implies lower grade), not a displayed matrix identity.

snippet.text:
structure Leading (B : F.Coeff →ₗ[ℂ] F.Coeff) (c : ℝ) : Prop where
  price : 1 ≤ c
  cap (i j : F.Index) : ‖B (column F j) i‖ ≤ c
  diagonal (i : F.Index) : 1 ≤ c * ‖B (column F i) i‖
  triangular (i j : F.Index) (hN : j ≠ i) : B (column F j) i ≠ 0 → (F.grades j).1 < (F.grades i).1

proof_context.conclusion: A leading map has a nonzero bounded diagonal and is triangular: an off-diagonal entry B(column j)_i is nonzero only if grade j < grade i.

snippet.text:
lemma low_le {B : F.Coeff ≃ₗ[ℂ] F.Coeff} {c k : ℝ} (h : Leading B.toLinearMap c)
    (hk : ∀ y, μ (B.symm y) ≤ k*μ y) (x : F.Coeff) : μ (P x) ≤ k*μ (P (B x)) := by
  have he := inv_triangular_high e h (B x-P (B x)) (by rw [map_sub,project]; abel)
  rw [map_sub,map_sub,LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply] at he
  rw [sub_eq_zero] at he
  exact le_trans (le_of_eq (congr_arg μ he)) ((size_low _ _ _).trans (hk _))

proof_context.conclusion: Triangularity makes B and its inverse preserve the kernel of the low-degree projection, giving mu(Px) <= k mu(P(Bx)).
